newsitem.title: CROATIA: Unilever has long-term plans in Croatia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Unilever has long-term plans in Croatia - paper.

text.p: Cosmetics-to-detergents giant Unilever UNC.AS has made plans for a long-term expansion in Croatia, a local newspaper quoted branch director Marcel Kerkmeester as saying on Wednesday.
"If you look at other countries, Unilever always wants to be a dominant player on the market," Kerkmeester told daily Vecernji List in an interview.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
In the interview Kerkmeester said the company was hoping to find local staff and give them adequate training to form what he described as "the best organisation in this region".

He was quoted as saying the company's plans to secure a leading market position also included acquisitions, but added that sluggish privatisation was delaying this. A proposed profit tax increase to 35 from 25 percent also worried the company.
Unilever, which has been present in Croatia through a local sales representative for the past five years, now has an office with 11 employees.

With a view to improving distribution it has entered cooperation with private Globus Group, which owns a chain of supermarkets Diona, and now plans to launch an extensive advertising campaign to promote its products.
Kerkmeester said Unilever was fairly content with current sales, which increased several times since 1995 but declined to mention any figures.
But he stressed it still had to boost its position in the face of similar imported goods and strong domestic competition.

"There is Saponia with its detergents and Pliva with toothpastes. We are aware that consumers aren't only waiting for us with our products," he added. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
